item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-efa5ac0eb9a1de0b","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"Amnesty reported that Chinese authorities continued restricting speech, association, and peaceful assembly, using national-security justifications; people faced arbitrary detention and unfair trials, including human-rights defenders. It also reported record youth unemployment of 21.3% among 16–24-year-olds and a lack of transparency surrounding senior-official disappearances and the former premier's death.","question_ids":["3B.5","3B.8","4B.3","4B.6","6B.5","7B.2"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The report covers China during 2023; the national indicators and institutional findings are directly period-relevant, while some underlying cases began earlier.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the conduct to Chinese authorities and, in a later section, specifically records Xi Jinping's August Xinjiang instruction; it does not establish that Xi personally ordered every cited act.","limitations":["Amnesty's assessment is an external human-rights organization's finding; the supplied excerpt does not provide the government's response."]},{"source_id":"SRC-efa5ac0eb9a1de0b","start_unit":4,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"In 2023, authorities continued harassing or detaining White Paper and related protesters; a Uyghur student, Kamile Wayit, was sentenced to three years for allegedly posting a White Paper protest video. Proposed Public Security Administration Punishments Law amendments would prohibit undefined conduct, clothing, or speech deemed harmful to national spirit or feelings, and new online rules required current-affairs and international-politics posts to be truthful, sourced, and subject to increased identity disclosure.","question_ids":["3B.5","3B.8","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","7B.1"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"All listed measures and the sentence occurred or were announced in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The conduct is attributed to Chinese legislative, regulatory, judicial, and security authorities under Xi's government; personal Xi involvement is not separately demonstrated.","limitations":["The excerpt reports expert concerns about vagueness and privacy but does not state final legislative enactment or implementation details for the proposed amendment."]},{"source_id":"SRC-efa5ac0eb9a1de0b","start_unit":5,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"Authorities prosecuted or detained human-rights lawyers, journalists, activists, and NGO workers under broadly defined national-security or public-order offenses. Xu Zhiyong and Ding Jiaxi received 14-year and 12-year sentences in April; Chang Weiping received a three-and-a-half-year sentence after reporting torture; Li Yuhan received six-and-a-half years after prolonged detention with limited lawyer access and inadequate medical care.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","3B.8","4B.3","4B.4","4B.9","7B.6","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Sentences, detention conditions, and the April 2023 Anti-Espionage Law amendment are period-relevant, though several prosecutions originated earlier.","ruler_attribution":"Amnesty attributes the actions to Chinese authorities; the excerpt does not prove Xi personally directed each case.","limitations":["The torture and medical-care allegations are reported allegations in the source excerpt, not adjudicated findings."]},{"source_id":"SRC-efa5ac0eb9a1de0b","start_unit":6,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"Amnesty reported no evidence of progress in implementing UN recommendations on Xinjiang, continuing systematic repression and impunity; during Xi Jinping's August visit to Urumqi, he called on local authorities to intensify suppression of 'illegal religious activities.' The report also described arbitrary detention and unfair trials, concerns about forced labor, coercive Tibetan labor-transfer and resettlement programs, closure of minority-language schools, and forced boarding-school assimilation policies.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.5","3B.7","3B.9","3B.10","4B.7","6B.3","6B.8","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The findings and Xi's August visit fall within 2023; some detention systems and policies predate the period but were reported as continuing.","ruler_attribution":"Xi is directly identified as calling for intensified suppression in Xinjiang; other reported practices are attributed to Chinese authorities and local implementation.","limitations":["Amnesty's excerpt summarizes UN and other reporting and does not provide a complete official response or independently resolve all allegations."]},{"source_id":"SRC-efa5ac0eb9a1de0b","start_unit":7,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"Hong Kong authorities continued using the National Security Law and sedition provisions against democratic activists, journalists, and rights defenders. The 47-person national-security trial began in February; police detained at least 32 people around the June 4 memorial period without charges; authorities sought to ban a democratic protest song, issued arrest warrants and HK$1 million rewards for overseas activists, and prosecuted other speech and protest activity. Separately, Hong Kong courts issued favorable rulings on transgender identification and same-sex partners' parental, housing, property, inheritance, and relationship-recognition rights, although the government had two years to establish an alternative framework for same-sex relationships.","question_ids":["3B.5","3B.8","4B.3","4B.4","4B.7","4B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The prosecutions, detentions, warrants, and court rulings occurred in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The adverse conduct is attributed to Hong Kong authorities operating under the Chinese sovereignty framework; the favorable findings are judicial decisions, not necessarily Xi-directed policy.","limitations":["The excerpt does not establish the extent of Xi's personal involvement in individual Hong Kong prosecutions or judicial rulings."]},{"source_id":"SRC-65858cee925eb847","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"SIPRI reported that the 2023 nuclear-arms-control environment deteriorated overall, but discussions between China and the United States made modest positive steps. China remained one of the five NPT-recognized nuclear-weapon states, while none of the nuclear-armed states engaged in the Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons process.","question_ids":["1B.4","1B.8","1B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The overview explicitly assesses nuclear arms-control developments during 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The source describes China's state-level position and engagement; it does not identify Xi's specific decisions or distinguish China's conduct from that of other nuclear powers.","limitations":["The supplied excerpt provides no details on the substance of the China-US discussions, Chinese doctrine, command safeguards, or specific Xi orders."]},{"source_id":"SRC-90eb382a46bf59ae","start_unit":4,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"The chapter states that nuclear command-and-control systems, including in sophisticated nuclear-armed states, remain vulnerable to system and human error and increasingly to cyberattack; it also identifies continued nuclear-weapon possession, nonproliferation failure, and nuclear-energy expansion as major security challenges.","question_ids":["1B.3","1B.9","1B.10"],"polarity":"context","period_fit":"The chapter was published in 2023 but the quantitative arsenal figures cited are for mid-2022 and the claims are global rather than China-specific.","ruler_attribution":"No Xi- or China-specific action is attributed in the supplied accessible summary.","limitations":["The source does not provide a concrete 2023 event or institutional finding about Xi Jinping or China's risk controls; it is retained only as contextual evidence."]},{"source_id":"SRC-f66bc04f9125391b","start_unit":5,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"In July 2023, the ICRC, China's National Committee on International Humanitarian Law, and the International Academy of Red Cross and Red Crescent held a five-day IHL session in China with 40 participants from foreign affairs, the legislature, cultural administration, Red Cross, military, police, military industry, think tanks, and universities. The program covered IHL principles, humanitarian action, urban warfare, case studies, and policy, and a participating university announced a pilot master's course in international human-rights and humanitarian law.","question_ids":["1B.7","2B.4","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The event and announced course were in July and September 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The activity involved Chinese state-linked institutions and participants but does not show that Xi personally authorized, funded, or enforced the program.","limitations":["The source documents education and dialogue, not battlefield compliance, implementation outcomes, or disciplinary action."]},{"source_id":"SRC-9c899954116f97db","start_unit":5,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"Human Rights Watch reported that several White Paper protesters remained detained, charged, or unaccounted for in January 2023; four Beijing protesters were formally arrested for 'picking quarrels and provoking trouble,' two Shanghai protesters' whereabouts were unknown, and additional detentions or enforced disappearances were believed possible. Reuters could not independently verify all statuses, and authorities did not respond to its requests for comment.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.5","3B.8","4B.3","4B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The report was updated January 26, 2023 and concerned the late-2022 protests' continuing consequences during the target year.","ruler_attribution":"The arrests and reported detention practices are attributed to Chinese authorities; Xi's personal order is not established.","limitations":["Reuters expressly could not independently verify the status of the named individuals."]},{"source_id":"SRC-f7da23852f77c700","start_unit":1,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"The World Bank's 2023 report states that 184 million people, including 37 million refugees, lived outside their country of nationality and recommends rights-based, sustainable migration management, formal labor access, protection for refugees, and international cooperation. It provides global policy findings rather than a China-specific event, policy, or outcome.","question_ids":[],"polarity":"context","period_fit":"The report was published in 2023, but its figures and recommendations are global and not specific to China's 2023 governance.","ruler_attribution":"No action or finding is attributed to Xi Jinping or the Chinese government.","limitations":["No concrete China- or Xi-specific fact in the supplied units materially answers the listed lenses."]},{"source_id":"SRC-3be055e024382ce2","start_unit":3,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"A 2023 study of China's State Council ministers and vice-ministers under Xi Jinping found varied patronage patterns: political loyalty was only one form of patronage affecting personnel configurations, and the study also examined expertise and professionalization.","question_ids":["4B.5","5B.2","7B.5","8B.4"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The study was published in October 2023 and analyzes personnel under Xi's administration, but its empirical period is not specified in the supplied excerpt.","ruler_attribution":"The finding concerns the personnel system under Xi Jinping's administration; it does not establish that Xi personally made each appointment or that patronage necessarily produced unlawful self-dealing.","limitations":["The accessible summary does not provide the underlying sample, estimates, individual appointments, or causal findings."]},{"source_id":"SRC-4f3460e2e9077470","start_unit":14,"end_unit":15,"fact_summary":"In October 2023, a Chinese navy vessel reportedly shadowed and attempted to cut off a Philippine navy resupply vessel near Thitu Island, approaching within 350 yards. The Philippine military said the maneuver risked collision and endangered personnel; China defended the patrol as lawful and asserted sovereignty over the feature. Reuters described this as part of repeated attempts to monitor and block Philippine resupply missions.","question_ids":["1B.5","1B.8","2B.2","2B.5","2B.8","2B.10","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The incident and reported pattern occurred in October 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The conduct is attributed to a Chinese PLAN vessel and China's foreign-ministry position; the excerpt does not prove Xi personally ordered the maneuver.","limitations":["The account is based on competing national statements; the supplied report does not independently resolve the maritime-law dispute."]},{"source_id":"SRC-59643c6ea7609ac6","start_unit":15,"end_unit":16,"fact_summary":"In March 2023, China's legislature retained central-bank governor Yi Gang and finance minister Liu Kun beyond the official retirement age, while appointing Xi confidant Li Qiang as premier and Li Shangfu as defense minister. Reuters reported that retaining Yi and Liu signaled continuity, credibility, stability, professionalism, and financial dialogue, while analysts also identified deep structural economic problems and the challenge of reform.","question_ids":["5B.2","5B.3","8B.4"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The appointments and 2023 economic target were announced in March 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Reuters reports the appointments occurred under Xi Jinping's third administration and describes Li Qiang as a longtime Xi confidant; it does not establish Xi's individual role in each retention decision.","limitations":["The positive interpretations are analyst assessments, not observed long-term outcomes; the excerpt gives no later performance data."]},{"source_id":"SRC-79ff62bee574b782","start_unit":1,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"At the December 2023 Central Conference on Work Relating to Foreign Affairs, Xi delivered a speech and the conference adopted a comprehensive external-work program centered on Xi Jinping Thought on Diplomacy, centralized CPC leadership, sovereignty and security, Belt and Road cooperation, global governance initiatives, and building a 'community with a shared future for mankind.' It also directed stronger strategic planning, institutional reform, personnel development, coordination, and more science-based and proactive foreign work.","question_ids":["1B.1","1B.2","1B.4","2B.1","2B.7","8B.1","8B.2","8B.3","8B.4","8B.5"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The conference was held in December 2023 and sets the stated program for the current and upcoming periods.","ruler_attribution":"Xi directly delivered the address; the report is an official Chinese government account and presents the policy in favorable terms.","limitations":["The source documents formal goals and organizational directives, not independent verification of implementation, outcomes, or consistency with coercive actions reported elsewhere."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":["SRC-2af30a25aa9b483b"],"batch_limitations":["The supplied corpus contains several bibliographic or global-context pages rather than China-specific evidence. Facts are limited to concrete claims in the supplied labeled units and are not scores."]}
